themes_detail.label: Street noise explosion
themes_detail.summary: Street and sidewalk noise complaints surged to 48 this week, a 380% spike above the 10.0 weekly average over the prior 8 weeks (z-score: 11.21), representing a sudden and statistically extreme deterioration in outdoor noise conditions across Crown Heights.
evidence: 48 street/sidewalk noise complaints this week vs. 10.0 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (380% spike)
Z-score of 11.21 indicates extremely rare statistical event
Represents most significant spike among all complaint categories this week
reporting_angles: Door-knock reporting: what specific sources are generating unprecedented outdoor noise? (construction, street vendors, events, traffic)
Has NYPD been deployed to enforce noise ordinances; what enforcement gaps exist?

themes_detail.label: Damaged and dangling street trees
themes_detail.summary: This week, Crown Heights reported 6 damaged tree complaints (586% above 0.9 weekly average) and 3 dangling street sign complaints (1100% above 0.2 weekly average), suggesting recent weather damage or maintenance failures affecting public infrastructure.
evidence: 6 damaged tree complaints this week vs. 0.9 weekly average (586% spike, z-score: 5.53)
3 dangling street sign complaints this week vs. 0.2 weekly average (1100% spike, z-score: 6.35)
Parallel spike patterns suggest shared cause (weather event, deferred maintenance, or contractor negligence)
reporting_angles: Did a recent weather event (wind, storm) damage trees and signage across the district this week?
What is Parks Department response time for hazardous tree removal; are safety hazards currently unaddressed?

themes_detail.label: Indoor air quality degradation
themes_detail.summary: Indoor air quality complaints jumped to 13 last week, a 285% spike above the 3.4 weekly average over the prior 8 weeks (z-score: 5.57), indicating a potential widespread mechanical or environmental issue affecting residential units.
evidence: 13 indoor air quality complaints last week vs. 3.4 weekly average (285% spike, z-score: 5.57)
Timing coincides with broader HEAT/HOT WATER crisis (3,889 complaints over 90 days), suggesting HVAC/heating system failures
No Reddit or local news coverage yet; emerging signal may be underreported
reporting_angles: Are heating system failures and landlord unresponsiveness creating dual crises—inadequate heat AND poor indoor air quality?
Interview residents with IAQ complaints: CO exposure, mold growth, or HVAC breakdowns; are tenants in older buildings disproportionately affected?

themes_detail.label: Illegal tree damage spike
themes_detail.summary: Illegal tree damage complaints surged to 3 last week, a 1100% spike above the 0.2 weekly average over the prior 8 weeks (z-score: 6.35), suggesting either coordinated tree vandalism or unauthorized contractor work in the district.
evidence: 3 illegal tree damage complaints last week vs. 0.2 weekly average (1100% spike, z-score: 6.35)
Distinct from 'damaged tree' complaints (different category), suggesting deliberate harm rather than weather
Parallels dangling street sign spike, but different root cause (intentional vs. structural failure)
reporting_angles: Are developers or contractors removing or damaging street trees without permits as part of unreported construction work?
Interview Parks Department: are illegal tree damage cases being prosecuted; what enforcement capacity exists?

themes_detail.label: Unexplained general complaint surge
themes_detail.summary: General 311 complaints spiked to 45 two weeks ago, a 154% jump above the 17.8 weekly average over the prior 8 weeks (z-score: 6.62), indicating a broad, unspecified service failure or reporting surge whose root cause remains unclear.
evidence: 45 general complaints 2 weeks ago vs. 17.8 weekly average (154% spike, z-score: 6.62)
No specific complaint type identified; categorization suggests citizen confusion about which agency to contact or catch-all miscoding
Timing predates current week's noise and tree spikes; may represent early warning signal of systemic dissatisfaction
reporting_angles: Request 311 data clarification: what do 'general' complaints contain; are residents unable to classify their issues?
Survey recent community complaints: is there a perception of city agency unresponsiveness driving use of catch-all categories?
